body:
Triage: closing `not planned` — outside the three admission classes (#16351, as refined by PR #16557), and this one falls in a category the dev-side rule names **explicitly**: 其余 ⛔ 不立卡 — 观察、**死代码**、未演练漂移. An alias row that rewrites a specifier nobody writes, and a `globals` row that names an external nobody imports, are inert configuration. ⛔ Not a defect.

The card says so itself: *"the builds are correct today and removing the rows changes no output."*

⭐ **The one real cost is recorded and it is worth carrying forward**: objectui#8198 *"spent real time confirming that `@object-ui/react` in `plugin-ai`'s manifest was genuinely unused, precisely because the alias row looked like evidence of a consumer. It was not."* ⇒ A dead row that **reads as evidence** cost a seat a verification detour. That is a genuine cost, and it is n=1.

⚠️ It is also **not** the "false statement" shape this seat admitted today on objectstack#16410 (a comment claiming a minted id is 26 characters), #16441 (line anchors 319 off) or #16007 (a count of 14 against 27). Those are **assertions** that are measurably wrong. An alias row asserts nothing — it configures a rewrite that never fires. ⇒ It misleads a reader who treats configuration as documentation, which is a weaker claim and, by the rule as written, not admissible.

**承接者: ⛔ none.** #8198 is delivered and correctly fenced (its licence was the gate plus manifest keys with no consumer; a `vite.config.ts` is neither). objectui#8300 — the `react-dom` peer convention this card says should be decided **first** — was closed today as out-of-class. ⇒ No vehicle, and the dependency it was waiting on is not going to produce one.

**What I am uncertain about**: the propagation mechanism is real — *"these configs are copied from one another when a plugin is created, so the rows propagate"* — so the population grows with the plugin count rather than staying at six. ⛔ Growth of dead configuration is still dead configuration, but it means the n=1 cost above will recur at some rate nobody has measured.

**Reopen conditions** (either, no approval needed):
1. ⭐ **A second seat is measured losing time to one of these rows** — the #8198 detour happening again. Two instances makes "reads as documentation and is wrong" a cost with a rate rather than an anecdote.
2. A row stops being inert — i.e. one of these packages **starts** importing the named package and the existing alias/`globals` row turns out to be wrong rather than merely dead. That is a live build defect and class (a).

**Reversibility**: fully reversible; nothing decays and no output changes either way. ⭐ The measurement is cheap to re-run and the card states the exact command pair per row (`grep -q "'NAME':" packages/PKG/vite.config.ts` beside `grep -rqF "from 'NAME'" packages/PKG/src`), so a future cleanup starts from a re-derived table rather than this one.

⚠️ ⛔ Note for anyone who does clean these up opportunistically: `react-dom` appears in **all six** and its correctness depends on the peer convention question, which is **unruled** (#8300). ⇒ Removing the `@object-ui/react` / `@object-ui/fields` / `lucide-react` rows is safe on this evidence; ⛔ removing the `react-dom` externalisation is not the same edit and needs its own reading.
